chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) said: My) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abu 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked

He was asked: 'By what did you recognize your Lord?' He replied: 'By the abolishment of resolve and the invalidation of ambition. I resolved, so My resolve was abolished; I had an ambition, so My ambition was invalidated.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam recognize God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the epistemological principle that true gnosis (ma'rifah) of God is not an intellectual acquisition but a divine bestowal resulting from the dissolution of human agency. By nullifying the servant's decisive will ('azm) and inner striving (hamm), God removes the veil of self, allowing the Divine to recognize Himself through the servant, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on the limits of human reason versus divine grace.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said: my father said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked,
“How did you recognize your Lord?’ He (AS) replied, “Through abolishment of decision and invalidation of ambition. My decision was abolished, and when I had an ambition it was invalidated.”
